sections.title: The Church in Jerusalem
sections.description: From the Ascension to Stephen's Martyrdom

sections.title: Judea and Samaria
sections.description: The Gospel Spreads to Samaria and the Gentiles

sections.title: Arrest and the Journey to Rome
sections.description: Paul's Imprisonment and Appeal to Caesar

events.title: The Ascension of Jesus
events.description: Forty days after the resurrection, Jesus ascends to heaven from the Mount of Olives while the disciples watch. Two angels assure them that he will return in the same way.

events.title: Matthias Chosen as an Apostle
events.description: The apostles cast lots to choose a replacement for Judas Iscariot. Matthias is chosen and counted among the twelve apostles.

events.title: Pentecost
events.description: The Holy Spirit falls upon the believers with the sound of a mighty wind and tongues of fire. Peter delivers his first sermon, and about three thousand people come to faith.

events.title: The First Church
events.description: The believers live in fellowship, share everything they own, break bread in their homes, and hold fast to the apostles' teaching. The Lord adds daily those who are being saved.

events.title: Peter and John Heal a Lame Man
events.description: Peter and John heal a man who had been lame from birth at the Beautiful Gate of the temple. Peter preaches to the crowd gathering in Solomon's Colonnade.

events.title: Ananias and Sapphira
events.description: Ananias and his wife Sapphira lie about the proceeds from a land sale and keep back part of it for themselves. Both fall dead after lying to the Holy Spirit.

events.title: Stephen's Martyrdom
events.description: Stephen, full of grace and power, delivers a long speech to the Council about Israel's history and accuses them of killing the Righteous One. He is stoned to death while seeing heaven opened.

events.title: Philip in Samaria
events.description: Philip preaches the gospel in Samaria with great success. Many come to faith and are baptized, including the magician Simon. Peter and John come down from Jerusalem and lay hands on them.

events.title: Philip and the Ethiopian Official
events.description: An angel sends Philip to the road between Jerusalem and Gaza where he meets an Ethiopian official reading Isaiah. Philip explains the Scripture to him, and the official is baptized.

events.title: Saul's Conversion
events.description: Saul is on his way to Damascus to persecute Christians when a bright light from heaven surrounds him. The risen Jesus speaks to him, and Saul is blind for three days before Ananias lays hands on him.

events.title: Peter and Cornelius
events.description: Peter receives a vision of a sheet with unclean animals and is sent to the Roman officer Cornelius in Caesarea. The Holy Spirit falls upon the Gentiles while Peter speaks, and they are baptized.

events.title: The Church in Antioch
events.description: Believers scattered after persecution preach the gospel in Antioch, also to Greeks. Barnabas brings Saul from Tarsus, and it is here that the disciples are first called "Christians".

events.title: Peter Released from Prison
events.description: King Herod Agrippa I arrests Peter and plans to execute him. An angel frees Peter from prison while the church prays for him. Shortly after, Herod dies, struck down by an angel.

events.title: Barnabas and Saul Sent Out
events.description: The Holy Spirit speaks to the church in Antioch during prayer and fasting, telling them to set apart Barnabas and Saul for missionary work. They are anointed and sent off.

events.title: Paul in Cyprus and Asia Minor
events.description: Barnabas and Paul preach in Cyprus, where the proconsul Sergius Paulus comes to faith. They travel on to Perga, Antioch in Pisidia, Iconium, Lystra, and Derbe, encountering both openness and resistance.

events.title: Return to Antioch
events.description: Paul and Barnabas return through the cities they visited, strengthening the disciples and appointing elders in each church. They go back to Antioch and report what God had done.

events.title: The Apostolic Council in Jerusalem
events.description: The apostles and elders meet in Jerusalem to discuss whether Gentile believers must be circumcised. Peter, Barnabas, and Paul give their testimony, and James proposes the decision: Gentiles should not be burdened with the Mosaic Law, but should abstain from food sacrificed to idols, blood, meat of strangled animals, and sexual immorality.

events.title: Paul and Silas Set Out
events.description: Paul and Barnabas disagree over Mark and part ways. Paul chooses Silas as his companion, and they travel through Syria and Cilicia to strengthen the churches.

events.title: Timothy Joins; The Vision of the Man from Macedonia
events.description: Paul meets the young Timothy in Lystra and takes him along. The Holy Spirit prevents them from traveling to Asia and Bithynia. In Troas, Paul has a vision of a man from Macedonia pleading for help.

events.title: Philippi: Lydia and the Jailer
events.description: In Philippi, the purple merchant Lydia comes to faith and is baptized along with her entire household. Paul and Silas are thrown into prison after driving out a spirit of divination, but an earthquake opens the doors. The jailer and his household are baptized.

events.title: Paul in Athens
events.description: Paul preaches in Athens and delivers his famous speech at the Areopagus. He begins with the altar "To an Unknown God" and proclaims about the Creator who now calls everyone to repentance.

events.title: Paul in Corinth
events.description: Paul arrives in Corinth and stays with the tentmakers Aquila and Priscilla. He preaches in the synagogue and establishes a large church. The Lord encourages him in a vision to remain in the city for a year and a half.

events.title: Apollos in Ephesus
events.description: Apollos, an eloquent Jew from Alexandria who knows the Scriptures well, preaches in Ephesus. Aquila and Priscilla take him aside and give him better instruction about God's way.

events.title: Paul in Ephesus
events.description: Paul arrives in Ephesus and works there for over two years. He teaches daily in the lecture hall of Tyrannus so that all in Asia may hear the Lord's word. God performs extraordinary miracles through him.

events.title: The Riot in Ephesus
events.description: The silversmith Demetrius starts a riot because Paul's preaching threatens the cult surrounding the goddess Artemis. The crowd fills the theater and cries out for two hours: "Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!"

events.title: Eutychus Falls from the Window
events.description: During a long evening speech by Paul in Troas, the young man Eutychus falls asleep and drops from the third story. He is taken up dead, but Paul throws himself on him and raises him back to life.

events.title: Farewell Speech at Miletus
events.description: Paul gathers the elders from Ephesus in Miletus and delivers a moving farewell speech. He urges them to shepherd the flock and warns against false teachers. Everyone weeps and embraces him.

events.title: Paul Arrested in the Temple
events.description: Jews from Asia recognize Paul in the temple and accuse him of bringing Gentiles into the holy area. A mob seizes him and tries to beat him to death, but the Roman commander intervenes.

events.title: Paul Before the Council
events.description: Paul is brought before the Jewish council and creates a division between the Pharisees and Sadducees by claiming that he stands accused because of the resurrection. The Lord appears to him at night and encourages him.

events.title: Paul Before Felix
events.description: Paul is taken to Caesarea and brought before the governor Felix. He defends himself against the charges and speaks about righteousness, self-control, and the coming judgment. Felix keeps him imprisoned for two years.

events.title: Paul Appeals to the Emperor
events.description: The new governor Festus suggests that Paul should stand trial in Jerusalem. Paul exercises his right as a Roman citizen and appeals to the emperor in Rome.

events.title: Paul Before Agrippa
events.description: King Agrippa II and Bernice hear Paul's defense speech. Paul testifies about his conversion and the resurrection. Agrippa says: "You almost persuade me to become a Christian."

events.title: The Shipwreck
events.description: Paul sails toward Rome, but the ship is struck by a violent storm for two weeks. Paul encourages everyone on board and assures them that no one will lose their life. The ship runs aground at Malta, but all 276 people on board are saved.

events.title: Paul in Rome
events.description: Paul arrives in Rome and is allowed to live by himself with a soldier as his guard. For two years he proclaims the kingdom of God and teaches about the Lord Jesus Christ with boldness and without hindrance.
